title: Knight against pawns
line: The knight is slow to cross the board, and a rook pawn is hardest for it.

steps.text: A bishop stops a pawn from across the board: this one can attack the pawn in a single move.
A knight has to come close to stop a pawn, one jump at a time. On the edge of the board it has the fewest jumps.
Tap every square from which a knight would attack the pawn.
steps.hint: Picture a knight on the pawn's square, and the squares it could jump to.
steps.after: Four squares, and only two are one jump from your knight.

steps.text: Stop the pawn: jump to a square that attacks it.

steps.hint: Two jumps can attack the pawn. Either will do.
steps.after: The knight attacks the pawn. If the black king guards it, the knight can give itself up for it, and the game is a draw.

summary: A knight stops a pawn only from close by, one jump at a time. Near a rook pawn it has fewest jumps.
